Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "The desktop uploader is installed on the records workstation beside the scanner, but it can also be used from the two review desks on the same office network. Its configuration is stored in the user profile, so each staff member can choose a download folder without changing another person's settings. The shared destination is a separate network location, and the uploader displays its full path before a transfer begins. Staff check that path against the folder name on the intake sheet, especially when two projects use similar names.

The first launch opens a connection panel with fields for the service address, account name, and authentication method. The service address is entered without a trailing slash because the uploader adds the required path automatically. The account name is the team's assigned login, not an employee's email address. Authentication uses the office credential manager, which prompts the user when a saved credential is missing or expired. The connection test checks access to the service but does not start an upload or alter files in the selected destination.

The transfer panel controls file handling. The maximum number of simultaneous transfers is set to three, which leaves enough network capacity for the scanner and the catalog system during busy periods. A smaller value can be used on the review desks if a large upload makes other work noticeably slow. The retry interval is measured in seconds, and the retry count applies to a failed attempt to contact the service. These settings do not change the number of times a user may deliberately submit the same file.

transfer.allow_resume

This option allows the uploader to continue an interrupted transfer from the last confirmed block rather than sending the entire file again. Staff leave it enabled for large image packages and check the service's transfer record before restarting a job manually. If a package changes while a transfer is paused, the uploader treats the changed file as a different transfer and begins a new validation. A resumed transfer still has to pass the service's final size and checksum checks; the option does not mark an incomplete file as successful.

The folder rules are reviewed before the first weekly batch. The temporary folder is on the workstation's local drive, while completed files go to the selected project folder on the network. The temporary folder needs enough free space for the largest expected package and any smaller files waiting in the queue. The uploader removes temporary fragments after a confirmed transfer, but it does not delete a source file from the scanner folder. A staff member can change the destination for a particular batch, provided the project folder has been created and the account has permission to write there.

1. For each batch, check the following items before selecting Start:
   a. Confirm that the project code on the intake sheet matches the destination folder.
   b. Open one sample file from the scanner output and confirm that it is not still being written.
   c. Compare the displayed file count with the count on the batch cover sheet.
   d. Check that the connection panel shows the expected service address and account.

The uploader shows a warning if a file has a name that already exists in the destination. Staff read the warning rather than relying on the file extension, since two files with different extensions can still contain versions of the same record. The available choices depend on the destination permissions and the service response. If the intake sheet says that an existing file should be retained, the staff member does not choose an overwrite option; the batch is paused while the project contact clarifies the intended file. The warning itself is not evidence that either file is the approved version.

During a transfer, the queue lists each filename, its current state, and the amount sent. A paused item can remain in the queue while another item continues, but a service-wide connection failure can stop all items. The status panel records the last contact time and the text of the most recent service message. Staff copy that message into the support ticket when asking for help, along with the uploader version and the approximate time of the interruption. They do not include passwords or credential-manager prompts in the ticket.

The log folder is configurable, but it should not be placed inside a project destination because project files may be moved or archived as a group. Log rotation is set to retain recent activity without filling the workstation drive. The logs include filenames, transfer times, and service responses, so access follows the same office rules as access to the intake records. A staff member can open the log from the Help menu and filter by date or batch code. Clearing a local log does not remove the corresponding transfer history held by the service.

Before closing the uploader, staff check that the queue is empty or that every remaining item has a known state. If an item is still running, they leave the workstation available until the status changes or follow the team's handoff procedure. If the office network is scheduled for maintenance, a batch that has not started is held until service is available; a batch already in progress is handled according to its displayed state rather than being restarted automatically.
